title: Stages of skill acquisition

draft.title: Stages of skill acquisition
card: A learner moves through three stages as a skill improves. Each stage describes how the learner is thinking and moving.
the first stage. The learner thinks about each step and makes many errors. Movements are often jerky and uneven.
the middle stage. The learner practises and refines the skill. There are fewer errors, and the learner can start to spot and fix some of them.
the final stage. The skill is automatic, so the learner can pay attention to other things, such as opponents or tactics.
draft.remember: Skill moves from thinking about every step, to refining it, to doing it without thinking.

a.q: Which description fits a learner in the associative stage of learning a skill?
opts: Practises often, makes fewer errors and refines the movement
Thinks about each step and makes many obvious errors
Performs the skill automatically while watching opponents
Has not yet tried the skill but knows the rules of the game
a.why: In the associative stage the learner practises and refines the skill, so errors become fewer. Thinking through each step belongs to the cognitive stage, which is the most tempting wrong option.
a.clue: This is the middle stage, after the basics are learned.

b.q: Jess has played netball for years. She now catches and passes without thinking, so she can watch where her teammates are moving. Which stage is she in, and why?
opts: Autonomous, because the skill is automatic
Associative, because she is still refining the skill
Cognitive, because she is paying attention to the game
Autonomous, because she has stopped making any errors
b.why: Jess does the skill without thinking about it, which means she is in the autonomous stage. Her attention is free for teammates. The last option is wrong because the stage is about the skill being automatic, not about never making errors.
b.clue: Ask where her attention is: on the skill or on the game around her.

a.best: Practises often, makes fewer errors and refines the movement

b.best: Autonomous, because the skill is automatic
